items.title: Robert Glasper interviewed by Greg Thomas, Clinton, New York, February 20, 2016
items.q: And that, and I was a part of that wave with Bilal’s band.

ctx.x: Now you said there was two waves, so that was one?

That was one wave. And that, and I was a part of that wave with Bilal’s band. We were going on tour with Erykah and Common and opening up for those guys, and the Roots and all this stuff. Then neo-soul kind of died down and then, not to toot my own horn, but when “Black Radio” came around I think that started another wave of college kids coming up and doing their own thing. You know? That’s why you have groups like The Internet and people from Berklee, even Internet, Hiatus Kaiyote, Snarky, all these other…

Grammy, which never happened, an instrumental band has never won and R &B Grammy before, in the history of it. You know what I mean? And so when we won that everybody googled who are you, first of all, you know. But then they listened to it and they were just like oh, and people kind of became open to it. That’s why you see all these other bands now coming into those categories and stuff. And it’s another wave of music that’s all doing that. It’s amazing to see.
